candidates.topic: The Zip Code That Does Not Exist — 00000
candidates.teaser: There's a zip code that officially doesn't exist — but thousands of real people are trapped inside it.
candidates.video_title: The Zip Code That Traps Real People
candidates.video_description: ZIP code 00000 doesn't officially exist in the US postal system, yet thousands of Americans are stuck with it on federal records. It began as a data-entry default and quietly became a bureaucratic nightmare for people trying to prove who they are.
candidates.script: Thousands of Americans are officially listed as living nowhere. Their zip code on government records reads 00000 — a code that doesn't exist. It started as a blank default field in federal databases, but once it was entered, it couldn't easily be corrected. These people get rejected by banks, hospitals, and employers — all because a computer filled in a zero. So right now, someone is trying to prove they exist, and a spreadsheet is winning.

candidates.topic: The Volcano That Changed Human History — Toba Supervolcano
candidates.teaser: 74,000 years ago, a single eruption nearly deleted every human being on Earth.
candidates.video_title: The Eruption That Almost Erased Humanity
candidates.video_description: The Toba supervolcano erupted roughly 74,000 years ago in what is now Indonesia, triggering a volcanic winter that may have reduced the entire human population to just a few thousand individuals. Some geneticists believe every person alive today descends from that tiny surviving group.
candidates.script: Every single person alive today might descend from a group smaller than your high school. Around 74,000 years ago, the Toba volcano in Indonesia erupted with a force 5,000 times greater than Mount St. Helens. It blanketed the sky for years. Genetic evidence suggests the entire human population crashed to as few as 10,000 individuals. We were nearly gone. One volcano almost ended the story before it started.

candidates.topic: The Color Your Eyes Can't See — Stygian Blue
candidates.teaser: There's a color your brain can produce that physically cannot exist as light.
candidates.video_title: The Color That Cannot Physically Exist
candidates.video_description: Stygian blue is a color that the human brain perceives under certain visual conditions, yet it corresponds to no wavelength of light that can actually exist. It is darker than black while still appearing vividly blue — a genuine perceptual experience with no real-world equivalent.
candidates.script: There is a color your brain can see that cannot exist in real life. It's called Stygian blue — bluer than blue, yet darker than black. No light source can produce it. It only appears when you stare at a bright yellow patch for 30 seconds, then look at a dimly lit blue surface. Your visual system manufactures something physically impossible. Your eyes are showing you a color that doesn't exist. What else are they making up?

candidates.topic: The River That Flows Uphill — Amazon Reverse Flow
candidates.teaser: Deep underground, the Amazon River flows completely backwards — and it's almost as big as the one above it.
candidates.video_title: There's a Second Amazon — And It Flows Backwards
candidates.video_description: Beneath the Amazon River lies the Hamza River, an underground waterway roughly the same length but four times wider. Discovered in 2011, it flows in the opposite direction at an almost imperceptibly slow pace through porous rock, eventually draining into the deep Atlantic Ocean floor.
candidates.script: There's a secret river buried beneath the Amazon — flowing the opposite direction. Scientists discovered it in 2011 and named it the Hamza River. It runs nearly 6,000 kilometers through porous rock, four times wider than the Amazon above it, moving so slowly it barely registers as flow. It drains silently into the ocean floor. Two of the world's largest rivers, stacked on top of each other, going opposite ways. The Amazon was hiding its twin.

candidates.topic: The Man Who Measured the Earth With a Stick — Eratosthenes
candidates.teaser: A man calculated the exact size of the Earth in 240 BC — using nothing but a stick and a shadow.
candidates.video_title: He Measured the Entire Earth With a Stick
candidates.video_description: In 240 BC, the Greek scholar Eratosthenes calculated the circumference of the Earth with remarkable accuracy using only the angle of shadows in two different cities on the same day. His result was within 2% of the value we use today — without satellites, without computers, without leaving Egypt.
candidates.script: In 240 BC, a man calculated the size of the entire Earth — and he never left Egypt. Eratosthenes noticed that on the same day, a vertical stick cast no shadow in Syene but a clear shadow in Alexandria. Using the angle difference and the distance between the two cities, he calculated Earth's circumference as roughly 40,000 kilometers. Modern satellites give us 40,075. He was off by less than 2%. With a stick.
